verse.reading: We will stop the wind in the coppersmith's cave, kindle fire in the blacksmith's forge, make gold on the head of those who spoke, make learning equal ... ; we will burn away the bond of women, see the mark of the true Thing and reach what we desired; not babbling, not babbling, staying still, we joined Parapara.
verse.nuance: கால் is both leg and wind: stopping it in the cave is the breath held. The smithy and gold-making are the alchemist's tools, which the stanza may mean literally or as inner work. Line four is obscure. The close, பன்னாதே, சும்மா இருந்து, puts silence above all the furnace-work.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: When will I meet straight, going through the moon's boundary, instead of letting the mind run loose to many places and not watching it?
verse.nuance: நிலவரை splits two ways: நிலா வரை, the moon's region or boundary (the moon-hall of 97, at the crown), or நில வரை, the limit of the land. With the cipher of the surrounding verses the first is likelier; நேர்படுவது, meeting straight or coming into line, is the mind's arrival after its scattering.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: Knowing it for ourselves as turmeric smeared on a pot of filth, as a coloured skin over a swarming nest of worms, as stinking mud in a pit of water, we threw it away; dance.
verse.nuance: The three images answer the three kinds of flattery: the painted surface, the skin, the wet hollow. தான் அறிந்து, knowing it oneself, is the ground of the renunciation; the Siddhar does not cite a text.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: When will I stand without obstruction in the sushumna that moves between ida and pingala, and stay there unshaken?
verse.nuance: The three channels are named plainly, which makes this the key to the ciphered 144. சலித்தருப்பது is corrupt or unusual: சலித்து can mean to be wearied or to be shaken, so the sense is either 'to remain without being shaken' or, less likely, 'to stay there and tire'; தடை அறவே (without obstruction) favours the first.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: With mind on the five letters, son, properly changing them head to foot and foot to head, the deities of the adharas come purely and, as told, stand sweetly in the heart; meditating thus with devotion, firmly smearing ash as the ground, if you do this daily, the unstable gross body becomes stable.
verse.nuance: The promise is kaya-siddhi: the body that does not stay is made to stay by mantra, meditation and ash. ஆதார தேவதைகள் are the presiding deities of the adharas, who are said to take their stand in the heart rather than in their own centres.

finding.claim: Loophole-free Bell tests confirm that entangled particles show correlations no local hidden-variable theory can explain, though these cannot be used to send signals.

verse.reading: The thought that runs about: catch it without letting it run, gather it and set it right; seek, and fit it to the arrow; set it within the wide open space of nada's end.
verse.nuance: அம்பு, the arrow, recurs in 2287 (அம்பு பூணும்); tradition reads it as the fixed inward gaze or the straight breath. நாதாந்த வெட்டவெளி, the bare open space at the end of sound, is where the mind is to be lodged; the stanza is the song's one positive method, framed in the same imperatives as its prohibitions.

finding.claim: Meditation programmes produce moderate improvements in anxiety, depression and pain, with low or no evidence of benefit for attention, mood or sleep beyond active controls.

verse.reading: They bend their effort to melting the lingam, not knowing the lingam of the right kind; the tale of joining lead with gold, is it not a disgrace, girl?
verse.nuance: லிங்கம் here is the alchemists' word for cinnabar (ரசலிங்கம், சாதிலிங்கம், red sulphide of mercury), and சாதிலிங்கம் is that mineral's name; the stanza plays on the word's other sense, Siva's emblem, so a second reading has them melting idols while not knowing the true linga. வங்கம் is lead or tin, and the gold-and-lead story is the coiner's fraud.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: Listen, son Vasimuni: in the thousand verses he gave earlier he told truly the drugs, salts, bound and melted substances and the way of gems, without a lie; in this book he will tell all the silence in order, so listen bowing.
verse.nuance: The disciple is வாசிமுனி, the breath-sage, and later வாசிநாதா; the name makes the pupil the breath itself. The earlier ஆயிரம் is an alchemical work claimed as Kakapusundar's; the verse marks the turn from alchemy to மவுனம், which the formulas of 2397 to 2403 then undo.

finding.claim: Whether adult humans make new hippocampal neurons is disputed, with major studies reporting both near-absence and abundance.

verse.reading: The bliss of the letter that was uttered as 'kū': millions say 'yogi, yogi' and never come to know and see it; the monkey mind swelling here and there like a palm, millions upon millions remain saying 'the One, the One'.
verse.nuance: ஆகிகூவென்று is obscure; கூ is one of Sivavakkiyar's cipher syllables (with கீ, ஊ, ஈ), which tradition takes as names for the breath or the mantra's parts. மனக்குரங்கு, the monkey mind, is the common image for restlessness. பூகம் (areca palm) is likely a tall, swaying thing; the line may be corrupt.

finding.claim: Meditation programmes produce moderate improvements in anxiety, depression and pain, with low or no evidence of benefit for attention, mood or sleep beyond active controls.

verse.reading: Thinking on the letter with the curl, setting it at the mouth of speech, passing beyond pain and pleasure, going through the channel they speak of, raising the fire of the firm akshara, and crossing the six lotuses, in the space beyond ...
verse.nuance: The sentence runs on into 1194. சுழித்ததோர் எழுத்து, the letter with a curl, is taken by tradition as Om (or its ஓ); அக்கிரம் may be அக்ஷரம், the letter, or அக்ர, the tip or crown; the fire raised and the six lotuses crossed are the serpent power and the six supports in the yogic body. The verse describes an ascent through the central channel in the Siddhars' usual terms without naming them.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: After praising the Lord of Pugali whose fame shone in the twelve ages past under different names, the bull-rider, husband of Uma, who bent the mountain and burnt the three cities of the strong-shouldered demons, with young moon on his growing hair and the single eye in his forehead that glared at Kama, the beginning the gods do not know, the poet confesses: in my untaught heart base understanding followed me, and with the empty gaze that looks and forgets, each time I looked, everything everywhere, mine and others', the many that come to be and the many that perish, what goes, comes and passes, more numerous than the sand heaped in the clear-watered world, the non-existent seeming to be and the existent unseen, I lay for many days in darkness; and the way it shook me was like a man who cannot see with his eyes and reels, the pit becoming his road and the road a pit, stumbling without end from one into the other; so it came, until I gained by compassion your look of growing grace, and then everything appeared false to me and you alone, the rare one, appeared true: like the many carved and painted shapes a master painter drew to catch a likeness, which to those who run their hands over them all without stopping show themselves as one wall.
verse.nuance: Two images carry the verse: the blind man for whom pit and road exchange places, which is the unenlightened state, and the painted wall, which is the enlightened one: the painter's many figures differ to the eye but the hand that feels them finds one surface, so the many things are false and the one substrate true. இல்லன உளவாய் உள்ளன காணா is the plain statement of maya in the Vedantic sense. The prose line printed after the verse (சடமாகிய உடம்பு எனக் கொண்டு, கல்லா உடம்பு எனவும் பாடமோதுவர்) is an editor's note that some read கல்லா உடம்பு for கல்லா உளத்தின்.

finding.claim: A model holds that psychedelics relax the brain's high-level prior beliefs, letting bottom-up signals revise entrenched self-models.

verse.reading: Like a deer that takes a mirage for water and goes after it, fools see the life of this earth and rejoice; those who have seen the higher state do not talk empty bluster, but seek the feet of the True One; dance.
verse.nuance: The mirage-deer (கானல்மான்) closes the section on possessions by naming the error: not that wealth is bad but that it is not what it seems. மேனிலை கண்டார், those who have seen the higher state, are set against the வீம்பு (vaunting) of the world, which sits uneasily with the Siddhar's own boasts in 2005 to 2013.

finding.claim: On the predictive-processing account, perception is the brain's best guess about the causes of sensory input, constantly corrected by prediction error.

verse.reading: Teacher who gladly gives to every living thing from the elephant to the ant: hunger presses hard on me, sinner that I am, Lord; it grips and wrings my ruined belly, Karonar.
verse.nuance: The appeal is from the universal feeder to the one belly left out, and the belly is called பாழ் வயிறு, waste, as if hunger itself were a fault of the body. Read beside 416, where the poet refuses to go to food, the verse is the cost of that refusal.

finding.claim: Fasting strongly induces autophagy in animal tissues, but direct evidence that it does so in human tissues is sparse.

verse.reading: Will the place where that inquiry dries up not come to me? Will the place where the inquiry one speaks is lost not come to me?
verse.nuance: விசாரம் is both worry and inquiry (vichara); அன்ன விசாரம், that inquiry, may refer back to the questions of 501 or to the mind's worrying in general. சொன்ன விசாரம் தொலைதல், the loss of the inquiry that is spoken, reads best as the end of doctrinal questioning, which the சொல் of 498 and 504 supports.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

tamil: என்னை என்னிலே மறந்தே இருந்த பதியும் மறந்து
தன்னையும் தானே மறந்து தனித்து இருப்பது எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: Forgetting me within myself, forgetting even the Lord who was there, forgetting myself by myself, when will I be alone?
verse.nuance: Even the Lord (பதி) is to be forgotten, which puts the state past worship and past 161's plea that he never leave. தனித்து இருப்பது is the solitary state, the kaivalya of yoga.

finding.claim: Agreement between practitioners reading the pulse in Ayurvedic and Chinese medicine is low to moderate, and the methods remain poorly standardised.

verse.reading: In the chakra of the worlds, in the space of the lord of the elements, the wind packed within the fire of the swelling lamp; at the gate where the two, sun and moon, move, changing the staff and climbing up, in the sporting space ...
verse.nuance: The stanza has no finite verb and seems to be the first half of a sentence that 1291 finishes. தவன and சோமன், sun and moon, are the right and left channels on the yogic reading tradition gives; தண்டு, the staff, is the spine; the space where the two play is the central channel. The wind packed in fire is the breath held at the root.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

tamil: நாலாம் பதம் தேடி நான் பெறுவது எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I seek the highest state, set the true reality within, seek the fourth state and gain it?
verse.nuance: நாலாம் பதம், the fourth state, is turiya (beyond waking, dream and sleep) in the avastha scheme, or sayujya, the fourth and highest of the graded releases; மேலாம் பதம் may be the same thing or a step above it. The verse keeps the ascent in steps rather than naming the end.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: One can stay, one can stay on earth; one can push away even the seven worlds of Hari, Mal and Brahma; in the pit that takes no embryo, in the pillar without legs, once the fire-chamber has been opened, you and I are the Lord.
verse.nuance: The pit that does not conceive and the legless pillar are coded: tradition reads the root centre and the central channel, and நெருப்பறை, the fire-chamber, as the kundalini fire. On that reading the verse promises long life on earth and mastery over the worlds, then union. 'You and I' may be the poet and the Lord, or the poet and a disciple.

finding.claim: Trained practitioners of breathing and cold exposure or of tummo meditation can voluntarily raise body temperature or modulate the innate immune response, effects once thought impossible.

verse.reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
verse.nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: Though your greatness is beyond measure, you stand shrunk small within my heart and do not leave; though you are body beyond body, the whole earth is called your form; though you are not within reach, you do not fail the distinction those who love you ask for; though by what is said you are no one's companion, you are the master who gathers the good lives; though you are everywhere, you are no refuge to those in whom deceit stays. Beyond that: the birthless birth, the growthless greatness, the renunciationless renunciation, the unlinked link, the unenjoyed enjoyment, the unsubtle subtlety, the undeparting departure, the unapproaching nearness, the undone deed, the unexcelled excellence; hot and cool, exalted and light, red and green, white and black; you make and destroy the many things that are, you remove and gather, you leave and reach: these and the countless other qualities bewilder each time they are thought, Lord of Otriyur girt by the high sea, so that unless those who say this here shrink their standing in words, who on the wide earth knows your nature?
verse.nuance: The paradox pairs (பிறவாப் பிறவி and the rest) are the poem's doctrine: every predicate of the Lord cancels itself. The close draws the consequence for speech, சொல்நிலை சுருங்கின் அல்லது, only by shrinking what one stands on in words can he be known. The one ethical line in the list is that he is no refuge to the deceitful (வஞ்சனை தங்கியவர்), which 963 repeats.

finding.claim: Loophole-free Bell tests confirm that entangled particles show correlations no local hidden-variable theory can explain, though these cannot be used to send signals.

verse.reading: When will the light of the eye leaping, the grasping of the intent, and the seeing of the light of the sky all be revealed?
verse.nuance: Three events are listed as past (பாய்ந்ததுவும், கொண்டதுவும், கண்டதுவும்) and their making-manifest is asked for: the poet has had the flashes and wants them to become open sight. In the yoga reading the eye-light is the brow centre and the sky-light the crown; plainly they are glimpses.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: To all the men who, born human among the seven births that Brahma, son of Vishnu, arranged, do not bow at the flower feet of the mountain daughter's lord and reach the Siva-state but delight in women and celebrate love, the poet speaks, and bids the blind-eyed listen: the soles that toil over thorns and stones they call cotton; the shins that are white bone they praise as leaping varal fish; the thighs of flesh and bone they call plantain stems; the waist that carries the long body they call a drum; the belly rolling with excrement, urine, slime and wrinkles they call a banyan leaf; the breasts that spread like a spider's web, swell, ooze, are scratched by nails, dry, shrink and hang for people to laugh at they call lotus buds, 'I say this to the blind of lust'; the hands that stretch, fold, take goods, feed and knead they call kanthal flowers; the neck of sweat and grime they call the areca palm; the hot and foul mouth they call the murukku flower; the teeth that chew rice and curry they call pearls; the sharp nose that drips water and mucus they call the kumizh fruit; the eyes that run with water and rheum they call water-lilies; the ears where wax rots they praise as vallai stalks; the hair on the skull, where lice and nits breed if oil is not combed in, they call a dark cloud; and saying such things in praise they go to the gate of hell they desire, the pit of lust where skin and flesh ooze pus, the field where embryos grow, the way the menstrual flow passes, the holed gate, the great road down which the eight-span body comes, the hidden place where earthly lust is spent, the gate where the dog of lust sits desiring, the sluggish road where those without the grace of the moon-crested one linger, the sore they cover with a cloth saying 'this is a wound', the rich sore that sounds with running water, the way the deluded enter and the sick never leave, the pit the proud lechers fall into, the great road by which woman and man are born, the water gate beside the gate where excrement falls: do not say this is sweet; bow instead at the twin feet of the one Lord of Kachi, who pities his devotees even for an offered leaf and grants the release of the Siva-state, lord of release, ageless First, who saw all the worlds in all the eggs, and give up praising the women of pleasure.
verse.nuance: The method is to quote the convention and then name the referent: each limb is given first as function or matter (bone, sweat, mucus) and then as the poets' figure, so that the figure is convicted by what it covers. The second catalogue is unusually literal, and தூமைக் கடவழி, the way of the menstrual flow, uses the Siddhars' word for the womb's impurity; பெண்ணும் ஆணும் பிறக்கும் பெருவழி concedes that the same gate is the way of every birth, including the hearer's. The attack is on the eye and the convention, not on women as persons, though the text does not make that distinction itself. சிலந்தி போலக் கிளைத்து, spreading like a spider or its web, for the breasts' first growth is obscure; இடைகழி வாயில் is the vestibule gate. பச்சிலை இடினும், even for a green leaf offered, is the standard measure of the Lord's easy grace.

finding.claim: People across cultures locate distinct emotions in consistent regions of the body, suggesting feelings are partly constructed from bodily sensation.

verse.reading: The place where you stayed still, demon, is what was pointed to, I have told you; I do not know what maya this is, and I do not see even myself.
verse.nuance: The repetition of 1679's second half is followed by a confession: the poet does not know what the appearance is and cannot see himself. Not seeing oneself (என்னையும் காணேன்) may be failure or the goal, since 1711 denies the self altogether.

finding.claim: Meditation is associated with reduced activity in the default mode network and changed coupling between it and attention and control networks, with larger effects in experienced practitioners.

verse.reading: Look: rising at dawn, without hurry set the mind at the suzhumunai; when the sun and moon exchange and rise at the suzhumunai that is the womb, standing within the uvula without wavering, see it subside within the suzhumunai; of the sixteen, the eight and the four and the three, without scattering, join as one and go.
verse.nuance: பரிதிமதி, the sun and moon, are the right and left breaths in the Siddhars' cipher, and their exchange at the central channel is the practice; a plain reading, that sunrise is the hour, is also present in உதயத்தில் எழுந்திருந்து. கருவான சுழுமுனை, the suzhumunai that is the womb or seed, repeats the run's link between the yogic centre and conception. The arithmetic of sixteen, eight, four and three is from 2432.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: Firm great sage Agastya, listen: meditating on true Shakti, like the blaze of sun and moon, knowing the seat of the five agents, doing pranayama steadily, abiding at Pothigai which is the meaning of the sruti, mounting the vaasi of the kala of life's pleasant breath, with the mind made one standing at the whorl, take the untroubled drink of nectar.
verse.nuance: அமிர்தபானம் is the yogic nectar held to flow at the crown when the breath is raised, as the next verse's மதியமிர்தம் (moon-nectar) confirms; it is tradition's reading and the verse's own image. பஞ்ச கர்த்தாள் are the five agents of the five acts. Pothigai, Agastya's hill, is called the meaning of the Veda.

finding.claim: The idea that a fixed stock of breaths or heartbeats sets lifespan rests on a cross-species correlation; within humans, lower resting heart rate predicts lower mortality but slowing breath has not been shown to extend life.

verse.reading: I will speak: the left channel is the moonstone; the right channel is the sun from the first; when the light that stood lovingly in the middle departs and then becomes one without departing, that is release; for those who looked with love, this is moksha here; for those who do not see, what is there but a body of lust? As a test, draw the breath up in the left channel, hold it in the sushumna, and you will be entranced.
verse.nuance: The cipher is stated and then decoded within the verse: இடைகலை is the moon, பின்கலை the sun, and the middle light the sushumna where they unite. சோதனையாய், as a test, invites the hearer to try the kumbhaka and see; சொக்குவீரே (you will be stunned, or absorbed) is the promised result.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: In the root of the hard-to-reach Paramasiva, the place where the two lights rise and set; the sushumna, where the body's working ceases, becoming the pillar, stands settled as the light that is the true thing; in this way, worship the foot called the root at the place where the two times are no more, and see.
verse.nuance: இருசுடர், the two lights, are sun and moon, which in the cipher are the right and left breaths; the sushumna is where they rise and sink. இருநேரம் அற்றிடம், the place without the two times, may mean beyond day and night or beyond the two breaths. The first two lines are printed twice with small variants, which looks like a doubled couplet.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: Plant Adishesha himself in the middle, scatter mantra-charged ash to the four directions, and take the hooded ones in your hands and dance so that they spit out their fierce poison, Siddhars.
verse.nuance: The rite closes with the serpent at the centre, consecrated ash (மந்திரித்த நீறு) and the handling of cobras until they discharge venom, which is 2004's boast performed. On the traditional reading the centre is the suzhumunai and the poison the mind's passions; the stanza's own words are a charmer's.

finding.claim: Calculated decoherence times for neural quantum states are far shorter than neural processing times, a central objection to quantum-brain theories.

verse.reading: Chant 'Sivaayavasi' and this whole world is yours; chant 'Sivaayavasi' and everything is attainment; chant 'Sivaayavasi' and you may rule the sky; 'Sivaayavasi' itself becomes the fire with two heads.
verse.nuance: சிவாயவசி rearranges the five letters சி வா ய ந ம so that they end in வசி, which tradition reads as வாசி, the breath: the mantra is to be chanted on the breath. இருதலைத்தீ (two-headed fire) may be the breath burning at both nostrils, or the fire that burns both good and bad deeds. The closing verse of the work promises what the chapter has mocked when sold: the world, siddhi, the sky.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

tamil: எண்ணாத தூரம் எல்லாம் எண்ணி எண்ணிப் பாராமல்
verse.reading: When will I see and know as light within a mirror, instead of counting and surveying, over and over, all the uncounted distances?
verse.nuance: The contrast is between measuring what is far and seeing what is near: the image is at once in the mirror, as the light is, without the labour of range. The mirror is the mind or the inner eye in the tradition; the verse only gives the figure.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: Wanting to see, you climb seas and mountains; is that not egoism, people without understanding? If you wish it and hold the Lord's feet within the true body, the soul standing as the pillar becomes Siva itself.
verse.nuance: ஆணவம் is the Siddhanta name for the root impurity of self-assertion, and the verse calls pilgrimage itself an act of it. தாணு (pillar, Sthanu) is a name of Siva and here the soul standing firm; the last line says the jiva becomes Siva, stated flatly.

finding.claim: Emotion and the sense of self may arise as predictions about the body's internal state, extending predictive processing to interoception.

verse.reading: Praise without wearying, holding it in the heart without deceit, the radiant light that has passed beyond the three times.
verse.nuance: காலம் மூன்று are past, present and future; சாலமின்றி, without trickery, asks for a holding that is not show, and சலிப்பற, without weariness, one that does not flag.

finding.claim: Nearly every cell keeps a roughly 24-hour molecular clock entrained by light, and misalignment of these clocks is linked to metabolic and mental illness.

verse.reading: I have seen the thousand and eight circles and what stood within that circle; I have looked at the hundred and eight of the great wide world, and the doubt that clings to a dull mind is gone.
verse.nuance: The numbers carry the sense and are not explained. The thousand and eight circles are most often taken as the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown, and what stands within it as the Lord there; the hundred and eight of the world may be shrines, scriptures or a sacred count. On a plain reading the boast is that inner sight has settled what outward search left in doubt.

finding.claim: Experienced meditators are not reliably better than non-meditators at detecting their own heartbeats, despite reporting greater bodily awareness.

tamil: பீற்றற் து ருத்தியைச் சோறிடுந் தோற்பையைப் பேசரிய
காற்றிற் பொதிந்த நிலையற்ற பாண்டத்தைக் காதல் செய்தே
verse.reading: The oozing body, the obscene shed, the torn bellows stuffed with flesh, the leather bag into which rice is put, the unspeakable, unstable pot filled with wind: the poet loved it, carried it about and wandered.
verse.nuance: Five names for the body, each a container: a shed, a bellows, a bag, a pot. காற்றிற் பொதிந்த, packed with wind, names the breath as what the pot holds and what makes it unstable. The second and third agavals expand the catalogue to dozens of names.

finding.claim: The body replaces around 330 billion cells a day, mostly blood and gut cells, so its material is continually renewed.

verse.reading: To remove the three impurities, keep in thought, even at the hour when you drive the sheep, the triple void that lies beyond the reach of the three faculties.
verse.nuance: The sense turns on முப்பாழ். An editor's gloss takes it as the three mayas (bindu, mohini and maan, the pure, mixed and impure maya); in Tirumular the three voids are the states past speech where the soul comes to rest, and 1734 has just named Brahman as the void. On either reading the verse asks the herdsman to hold a nothing in mind while at work, so that the three malas fall away. செம்மறி ஓட்டிய வேலை, the time of driving the sheep, is the cowherd's working day.

finding.claim: A theoretical account proposes that meditation progressively loosens predictive models, from reduced mind-wandering to cessation of experience in advanced states.

verse.reading: Even if one sets arsenic in a crucible, feeds it with white milk, covers it with grass and gives it the north-east firing, what is there in it, girl?
verse.nuance: பாஷாணம் is the class of arsenical and other poison-stones; குகை is the covered crucible; புடம் the calcining fire, here of a named kind (ஈசானியப் புடம், perhaps by direction or by name). The stanza lists a real procedure only to ask what is gained; it is not a recipe and the text gives no quantities.

finding.claim: A scoping review found 220 cases of heavy-metal poisoning, mostly lead and mercury, linked to Ayurvedic and Siddha preparations, with most analysed samples over permissible limits.

verse.reading: What preceded Hari is the letter A; what stood within Hari is the five letters; what preceded holding is the five letters; and what stood within the breath-horse is the five letters.
verse.nuance: The stanza turns on அரி, which is Hari, Vishnu, but in cipher can be the sun or the letter; வாசிப்பரி is the horse that is the breath. Tradition takes the stanza to place the five letters in the breath, so that the mantra is breathed rather than said. தரிக்கும் (holding, or bearing) is unclear.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: What is a Paraiyar woman, what is a Brahmin woman? Is there a number marked on flesh, skin or bone? Is the pleasure of the one different, is the pleasure of the other different? Separate the Paraiyar woman and the Brahmin woman within yourselves and see.
verse.nuance: பணத்தி is read by tradition as the Brahmin woman (பார்ப்பனத்தி shortened), though literally it is a woman of money; the argument needs the two ends of the caste order. இலக்கம் இட்டு is a mark or number stamped on the body. The test is bodily, in flesh and in intercourse, not scriptural, and the verse asks for the distinction to be found inside the questioner.

finding.claim: Indian groups descend from a mixture of ancestral populations, and widespread intermarriage gave way to strict endogamy only about 1,900 to 4,200 years ago.

verse.reading: Teacher who gladly gives to every living thing from the elephant to the ant: hunger presses hard on me, sinner that I am, Lord; it grips and wrings my ruined belly, Karonar.
verse.nuance: The appeal is from the universal feeder to the one belly left out, and the belly is called பாழ் வயிறு, waste, as if hunger itself were a fault of the body. Read beside 416, where the poet refuses to go to food, the verse is the cost of that refusal.

finding.claim: Intermittent fasting improves metabolic markers in animals and some humans, but trials show weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction.

verse.reading: He is easy to see, and even when seen is not seen here; for those who set a noble mind on him, he is the light within the ruby.
verse.nuance: காட்சிக்கு எளியான் is the Kural's phrase for an accessible king, turned on the Lord. கண்டாலும் இங்கு காணான் is the paradox that seeing him is not seeing him as he is. மாணிக்கத்துள் ஒளி returns from 550.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.
